To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of micrometric aluminum powder to high-density polyethylene matrix does not deteriorate the performance of the composites and can be used to obtain materials with improved thermal conductivity.

the mechanical and thermal properties of the HDPE/Al composites can be enhanced by introducing up to 20 wt% of aluminum powder without the use of any pre-treatment of the filler, which can be considered beneficial in the engineering of PE-based composites.
the mechanical, thermal and rheological properties of polyethylene-based composites filled with micrometric aluminum powder are not deteriorated when the content of aluminum is higher than 10 wt%.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new class of polymer/metal composities that are characterized by the combination of the mechanical and thermal properties of the polymer matrix and the electrical conductivity of the metal filler.
the analysis of the impact of Al content on the properties of PE composites, which may be useful for the design and optimization of polymer/metal composite materials for various applications.
the possibility of obtaining PE-based composites with improved mechanical properties, without the use of additional additives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented study shows the possibility of the use of aluminum powder as a filler for PE-based composites.
the incorporation of aluminum filler in a PE matrix is possible, but the amount of aluminum should not exceed 20 wt% to avoid a significant decrease in mechanical properties.
aluminum is not a suitable filler for the HDPE matrix, and its incorporation should not be considered as a method of increasing the mechanical properties of the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mechanical and rheological properties of PE/Al composites were not affected by the addition of 5 wt% of aluminum, while the thermal properties of composites with a higher filler content (10 wt%) were improved.
the addition of aluminum powder to polyethylene matrix does not deteriorate the mechanical properties of the composites.

the addition of 1–5 wt% of aluminum powder to the high-density poly(ethylene) matrix is an effective method for the improvement of mechanical properties, without a significant deterioration of the rheological properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of PE-based composites filled with micrometric aluminum powder can be significantly improved by increasing the filler content up to 20 wt% without any additional treatment.
the incorporation of aluminum filler into the HDPE-based matrix does not significantly affect its rheological properties, and the obtained composites are suitable for injection molding.
it is possible to obtain a composite material with a high filler content, which does not deteriorate the mechanical properties of the polymer matrix.
